clauses.statement: TaskBoundRepoControlDecision may clear the independent repo-control unsafe signal only for an explicitly selected Task whose classification repo_control groups exactly cover every changed independent repo-control path and every declared repo_control group is dependency-graph connected to at least one declared non-repo-control group.

test_pattern.must_contain: TAR-CLI-001 pr prepare persists Task-bound repo-control proof

clauses.statement: Missing Task context, duplicate groups, unknown dependency IDs, partial exact coverage, extra changed repo-control paths, and any disconnected declared repo-control group retain unsafe_for_atomic_override true. Legacy Task groups with no classification remain loadable but cannot authorize repo-control scope. Once any target group declares classification, every group must satisfy the typed schema; malformed or partially typed canonical Task groups are rejected by pr prepare --task with the configured state path and repair guidance before scope assessment.

test_pattern.must_contain: TAR-INV-001 fail-closed malformed and incomplete Task graphs
TAR-CLI-002 malformed typed Task state is rejected with repair guidance
TAR-CLI-003 disconnected declared repo-control group remains unsafe
TAR-CLI-004 legacy untyped Task groups remain loadable

clauses.statement: Task path coverage uses exact repository-relative target_files strings and never infers coverage from globs, basenames, prose, or acceptance text.

An eligible Task proof persists Task ID, canonical Task state path, covered repo-control paths, covering repo-control group IDs, and dependency edges in machine-readable scope evidence and the split plan.

test_pattern.must_contain: TAR-CLI-001 pr prepare persists Task-bound repo-control proof

clauses.statement: Task eligibility does not bypass Story atomic metadata, generated-lane coverage, current-HEAD reviewer ownership, verification evidence, Gate status, strict target validation, or VibePro PR creation.

test_pattern.must_contain: TAR-INV-003 Task proof cannot bypass atomic authority

clauses.statement: Story-scoped preparation without a Task, the existing config-only registration exception, ordinary unsafe repo-control splitting, and strict target validation retain their prior behavior.

test_pattern.must_contain: TAR-INV-004 no-Task independent repo-control remains unsafe
pr prepare keeps every required verification command after current-head reviewers accept an atomic scope
TAR-CLI-005 strict target validation still rejects non-test files
TAR-CLI-006 config-only registration exception remains compatible through task-scoped pr prepare

diagrams.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> unsafe
  unsafe --> task_bound_reviewable: exact coverage and connected typed Task graph
  task_bound_reviewable --> atomic_blocked: Story or evidence incomplete
  task_bound_reviewable --> atomic_accepted: existing atomic contract passes
  atomic_blocked --> [*]
  atomic_accepted --> [*]
diagrams.rationale: TaskBoundRepoControlDecision changes only the repo-control signal; existing atomic authority remains a separate transition.
Task-bound repo-control analysis establishes only a reviewable candidate. Existing atomic authority independently decides whether the candidate may remain in one PR.

diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Malformed["malformed or incomplete Task state"] --> Parser["strict typed Task parser"]
  Extra["uncovered changed repo-control path"] --> Coverage["exact coverage check"]
  Disconnected["disconnected repo-control group"] --> Graph["dependency connectivity check"]
  Stale["stale review or verification"] --> Authority["current-HEAD authority check"]
  Parser -->|reject| Block["fail-closed / split recommended"]
  Coverage -->|reject| Block
  Graph -->|reject| Block
  Authority -->|reject| Block
  Parser -->|valid| Candidate["reviewable candidate only"]
  Coverage -->|complete| Candidate
  Graph -->|connected| Candidate
  Candidate --> Authority
  Authority -->|all current| Accept["atomic scope accepted"]
diagrams.rationale: Malformed, incomplete, disconnected, or stale evidence cannot elevate repository-control changes into atomic authority; every failure path remains fail-closed.
